FreeCell on NoCharge: Planning with Free Cells

A source-checked guide to NoCharge FreeCell: its face-up seeded deal, free-cell move capacity, and current V2 limits on undo and saved records.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 22, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

All cards visible. Plan your moves.

Play FreeCell SolitaireBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: FreeCell is a face-up sequencing puzzle. NoCharge’s current version shows a seeded 52-card deal, four free cells, four foundations, and the move-capacity rule; it does not save a win record.

All 52 cards are visible from the start in eight tableau columns. Four free cells can each hold one card, and four foundations build upward by suit from Ace to King. The puzzle is about freeing and arranging cards, not discovering hidden cards.

Use free cells as temporary space

A free cell holds one exposed card. Empty cells and empty tableau columns determine how many cards can be moved as a descending alternating-color run. The engine calculates the current limit as (empty free cells + 1) × 2empty tableau columns, excluding the destination column from the empty-column count.

For example, four empty free cells and one other empty tableau column allow a run capacity of ten cards. With no empty free cells and no spare empty column, only one card can move as part of a run. A card can still be moved directly to a legal foundation or empty cell when the rules permit it.

What the current controls do

Select an exposed card or a valid descending run, then choose a free cell, foundation, or tableau destination. Tableau runs descend by alternating colors; foundations ascend by suit. Invalid moves are rejected with a status message. The page shows a move count, but the current game has no automatic foundation move or Undo control.

Reset and records

Reset to seeded start restores the same face-up deal. The move count and board are in the active page session; NoCharge V2 does not save FreeCell wins, a best-move record, or a game history to browser storage or an account. There is no timer or winnability label.

For a deliberate first scan, look for buried Aces, useful empty columns, and long legal runs. The game does not grade that plan; it only accepts or rejects moves under the stated rules.
